conviction_note: The FY26 numbers themselves are arithmetically boxed in by a guide the company confirmed in May and the CFO re-anchored at a Goldman conference on 14 Sept, while the quarter being reported (Apr-Jun 2026) is the single best luxury quarter in three years and the stock sits 4% off its 52-week low with 3.95m shares short and ~32 days to cover; I put the asymmetry at about +3 points, deliberately small because the real event is the first-ever FY27 guide, which I have no read on.

findings.finding: LUXE's fiscal Q4 is the quarter ended 30 June 2026 — exactly the window in which Richemont reported group sales +20% at constant rates with online retail +18% (quarter ended 30 June 2026), Kering posted +2% comparable for its first positive quarter in three years, and LVMH's Fashion & Leather Goods returned to +1% organic for the first time in seven quarters, with double-digit growth from American shoppers; LUXE's own Q3 (to March) was flat ex-FX and management blamed 'geopolitical headwinds in March', so the demand comparison inverts inside the reported quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market had carried the sector inflection across to LUXE, the ADR would not be trading within 4% of its 52-week low ($7.155 against a $6.54-6.86 low) and -6.96% over 20 days while Richemont and Kering re-rated (Kering +15.9% on its own results day), and sell-side would not have cut targets into the print — TD Cowen $12 to $8, JPMorgan $10 to $9, consensus target from $10.38 to $9.25. The price is treating LUXE purely as an idiosyncratic restructuring, and the run-up and the put/call open interest of 2.17 both say the same thing. What is unpriced is that the Apr-Jun demand backdrop was a tailwind in precisely the quarter management had already guided NAP & MRP to return to growth in ('with growth in fiscal Q4, we expect Net and MR P to have net sales decline by only a mid-single digit for the full fiscal year', 19 May 2026) and the quarter in which THE OUTNET's drag was removed (sale closed 30 April 2026).
findings.independence: LVMH/Kering H1 2026 read on the same quarter, separate source: https://www.nssmag.com/en/fashion/46402/lvmh-kering-hermes-first-half-2026-results . The management Q4 growth statement is from the Q3 call transcript, https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/markets-news/Motley%20Fool/2023372/luxexperience-luxe-q3-2026-earnings-transcript/ (2026-05-19), which is also the source behind finding 3 — treat those two as one document cluster for that leg.

findings.finding: 3.95m LUXE shares are sold short against an average daily volume of roughly 109k-125k shares, i.e. 31.6 to 34.3 days to cover, on a reported free float of 17.19m shares out of 137.26m outstanding (Richemont alone holds 49,741,342 consideration shares) — an extreme days-to-cover for a $980m name going into a binary bmo print.
findings.why_not_priced: The sweep marked short interest 'unavailable' and the only figure it could date was a year-stale 2025-09-30 MarketBeat alert of 2.15m shares / 8.0 days to cover — so the position has roughly doubled in shares and quadrupled in days-to-cover since the last figure anyone in this pipeline had. The raw short number is public and semi-monthly, but what is not in the price is the interaction: the same baseline shows put/call open interest at 2.17 on only 714 contracts, so the hedging that would normally absorb a squeeze is not there, and a stock cannot simultaneously price 32 days of covering demand and sit 4% off its 52-week low. If the market had priced it, the ADR would carry a borrow-driven premium rather than the recent -6.96% drift.
findings.independence: Finviz independently shows 3.96M short and a 31.64 short ratio on 125.15K average volume, https://finviz.com/quote?t=LUXE (retrieved 2026-09-15). Caveat I will not hide: the 17.19m float figure is from the same stockanalysis page as the short number and I could not corroborate it; the days-to-cover figure does not depend on it and is the part two sources agree on.

findings.finding: The FY26 headline is arithmetically pre-determined: H1 FY26 GMV was EUR1,230.6m and Q3 segment GMV sums to EUR653.7m (Mytheresa 279.6 + NAP&MRP 243.4 + YOOX 130.7), so against the confirmed FY26 guide of EUR2.5-2.7bn GMV, Q4 needs only about EUR616m versus a EUR654m Q3 run-rate to clear the bottom; on margin, 9M adjusted EBITDA is about EUR0.9m on EUR1,838.8m of net sales (+0.05%) against a -1% to +1% FY guide, and the CFO said on 19 May that Q4 adjusted EBITDA would be 'similar to Q3 levels', then on 14 September told the Goldman Sachs Global Consumer and Retail Conference that Mytheresa had already delivered roughly a 6% adjusted EBITDA margin for FY26.
findings.why_not_priced: A CFO does not sit on a conference stage 48 hours before a print and volunteer a past-tense full-year segment margin if the print is about to break the guide; that is a de-risking event with a two-day half-life in a name with 109k shares of daily volume, and the tape has not moved on it (-2.79% over the last 5 days). The baseline's own 10.94% 'implied move' is flagged unusable (ATM bid-ask 67% of mid, 714 contracts of open interest), so nothing in the option market is expressing that the FY26 actuals are low-variance — the surprise capacity is concentrated in the FY27 guide, not the FY26 number, and that is a different distribution from the one a generic 11% straddle implies.
findings.independence: The Q3 FY26 release is the source for the confirmed guide and the Q3 segment GMVs, https://investors.luxexperience.com/news/news-details/2026/Q3-FY26-Results-LuxExperience-Group-Reports-Positive-Adjusted-EBITDA-Profitability-for-the-Second-Consecutive-Quarter-Confirming-Full-Fiscal-Year-2026-Guidance-as-Transformation-Plan-Is-Fully-on-Track/default.aspx (2026-05-19); the H1 GMV is from the corrected Q2 release, https://investors.luxexperience.com/news/news-details/2026/CORRECTING-and-REPLACING-Q2-FY26-Results-LuxExperience-Group-reports-Net-Sales-growth-of-5-7-ex-FX-and-return-to-Adjusted-EBITDA-profitability-fully-confirming-the-transformation-plan-targets-4f2057ca0/default.aspx (2026-02-10). Note the Q1 (EUR589.0m) and Q2 (EUR684.8m) standalone GMVs sum to EUR1,273.8m against the EUR1,230.6m H1 figure, a EUR43m inconsistency I cannot resolve; I used the lower H1 number, which is the conservative direction for this finding.

findings.finding: Both luxury sites are losing traffic rank through the quarter the FY27 guide will be written off: mytheresa.com's global rank fell from #6,112 to #6,699 over the three months to August 2026 with visits -6.5% month-on-month, and net-a-porter.com sat at global rank #7,675 in August 2026 with visits -8.11% month-on-month.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody builds a model of a $980m NYSE-listed Dutch ADR off Similarweb, and the sell-side previews that were cut in the last three months are anchored on the FY26 guide, not on July-August run-rate. If this were priced, the drift into the print would be steeper than -2.79% over five days and the target cuts would have referenced current trading rather than 'execution risks and valuation'. I am sizing it small on purpose: July and August are the seasonal trough for luxury e-commerce, so a mid-single-digit month-on-month decline is close to normal and only the three-month rank deterioration carries any information.
findings.independence: Same vendor, different property: https://www.similarweb.com/website/net-a-porter.com/ (August 2026 data, retrieved 2026-09-15). That is one source cluster, not two, and I am counting it as one finding.

searched_and_found_nothing: SEC EDGAR 6-K stream for CIK 0001831907 — nothing filed since 2026-05-19, so no quiet filing, no covenant or capital event, and no pre-announcement in the four months into this print

Richemont FY26 Annual Report and Accounts — the sweep pointed at the equity-accounted-investment note for a third-party read on LUXE's loss run-rate; the PDF would not render page-by-page in this environment and neither the 22 May 2026 results release nor any secondary source gave the euro share-of-loss or the carrying value of the 33-36% stake, so I dropped the angle rather than approximate it

A claimed slip in YOOX profitability timing — the 19 May 2026 call said '12 to 15 months' (i.e. May-Aug 2027) and the 14 Sept conference said 'by fiscal 2028' (July 2027-June 2028); those overlap, so there is no defensible slip and I dropped it

Insider transactions — LuxExperience is a foreign private issuer exempt from Section 16, so there are no Form 4s; the one 'insider' line surfaced by an aggregator (CEO Kliger, October 2025) could not be tied to a filing
Any lock-up expiry or disclosed sell-down by Richemont or MYT Holding LLC on the 49,741,342 consideration shares — no source found either way

Company news flow between 2026-05-19 and 2026-09-15 other than the 2026-08-26 earnings-date release — the IR news page would not enumerate and no press coverage of a product, partner, warehouse or brand-partner event surfaced
App-store review volume and rating trend for the Mytheresa and NET-A-PORTER apps
A current dated short-interest settlement figure from Nasdaq (503) or Market Chameleon (access denied); the 3.95m/3.96m figures are undated vendor snapshots taken 2026-09-15
baseline_tension: It cuts against the baseline on every readable axis — the run-up is -6.96% with the ADR 4% off its 52-week low and put open interest running 2.17x calls, and my read is that the downside is the crowded side into a print whose FY26 numbers are already boxed in by a confirmed guide; the honest counterweight is that the FY27 guide is the actual event, it is being given for the first time, and I have no evidence about it, which is why the number is +3.0 and not larger.
